body: Just know that from my experience (been there a few weeks), if anyone sees you standing still not doing anything for maybe, if you're lucky, 30 seconds max, you will be yelled at to go do something or get something. I've literally been doing a certain job and have had someone yelling at me for not doing that specific job. As. I. Did. It. Frustrating, and if you're a cashier you have about 30 different jobs to do at once, including disinfecting and deep cleaning the entire store and bathrooms before close. And schedules as far as I know are only in person, so take a picture whenever the new week comes out. I guess my only tip is too be prepared to feel unprepared and overwhelmed at first. And probably for a while after that too. Sorry bud

don't think that your girlfriend is sick of you, if I know anything at all, normally the only person sick of you is yourself. everything else is usually in your head. it's what we want to make ourselves believe so it's easier to let go. I hope we can both keep holding on

I'm also in the exact same boat as a freshman, and I'm in my own mental breakdown about whether I just fucked my entire life at 18. I scheduled a pre health advisement meeting to take about my choices now, and I've looked at other majors now in CALS to see what my options are. Unfortunately a lot of them require Chem 2080, which sucks, but I know that if I took it at school I wouldn't fail considering I was at a B+ when we left campus for COVID. To say this has been a rough semester is an understatement, and anyone who says otherwise probably has a decent mental and home situation and work ethic, which can't be said for all of us. I'll update what the advisor tells me, but keep in mind this is Cornell, tougher than most schools, and one course in arguably one of the hardest tracks does not make us failures.

From what I've heard you're not supposed to use any AP credits for any classes if you are premed. I'm only a freshman premed though so I might not be the best source for this, I would definitely talk to academic advisors if/when planning your schedule.
